cursor.definition: cursor ōris, m 1 CEL-, a runner, racer, competitor: Ut cursor frena retentat equi, O. — A courier, post, N.: per dispositos cursores nuntiare, Ta.—A lackey, errand-boy: Gaetulus, Iu.

cursus.definition: cursus ūs, m 1 CEL-, a running, course, way, march, passage, voyage, journey: cursum quom institeris, T.: navium, Cs.: ingressus, cursus, accubitio: cursu cum aequalibus certare, S.: cursu contingere metam, H.: se cur…

curto.definition: curtō āvī, ātus, āre curtus, to shorten, consume: Quantulum summae curtabit quisque dierum, H.

curtus.definition: curtus adj., shortened, mutilated, broken, short: vasa, Iu.: testa, O.: temone iugum, Iu.: Iudaei, i. e. circumcised, H.: equus, castrated, Pr.: mulus, with cropped tail, H.—Fig., lessened, impaired, defective, poor: …

curulis.definition: curūlis (curr-) e, adj. currus, of a chariot: equi, the horses provided at the public cost for the games, L.: sella, the curule chair, official chair (of consuls, praetors, and curule aediles), C., L.: ebur, a throne …

curvamen.definition: (curvāmen inis), n curvo, a bending, bend, vaulting (only abl sing., nom. and acc plur.): patriae curvamina ripae, O.

curvo.definition: curvō āvī, ātus, āre curvus, to crook, bend, bow, curve, round: Curvari manūs et crescere in unguīs, O.: flexile cornu, O.: lances, i. e. by its weight, H.: Fronte curvatos imitatus ignīs lunae, the flaming sickle, H.…

curvus.definition: curvus (-vos) adj. CVR-, crooked, curved, bent: aratrum, V.: hami, O.: falces, V.: rates, Pr.: litora, Ct.: flumen, winding, V.: aequor, swelling, O.: arator, stooping, V.: caelator, Iu.— As subst n.: curvo dignoscere…

cuspis.definition: cuspis idis, f a point, pointed end, blade, head: asseres cuspidibus praefixi, Cs.: acuta teli, O.: pro longā cuspide rostrum, sword-blade, O.—A spear, javelin, lance, V.: tremenda, H.—A trident (of Neptune), O.: trip…

custodia.definition: custōdia ae, f custos, a watching, watch, guard, care, protection: fida canum: dura matrum, oversight, H.: navium, Cs.: illa (sc. pontis), N.: aliquid privatā custodiā continere: suae custodiae causā habere, as a body…

custodio.definition: custōdiō īvī, ītus, īre custos, to watch, protect, keep, defend, guard: provinciam: tuum corpus: me civitatis oculi custodiunt: custodiri suspecta, be garrisoned, Ta.: castra, ne quis elabi posset, L.: ne qua manus se…

custos.definition: custōs ōdis, m and f SCV-, a guard, watch, preserver, keeper, overseer, protector, defender, attendant: corporis, a body-guard, L.: nostri, Cs.: portae: pontis, N.: cum custodibus venire, under guard, S.: gregis, V.: …

cuticula.definition: cutīcula ae, f dim. cutis, the skin, Iu.

cutis.definition: cutis is, f SCV-, the skin, H., O.: pro cute pellis, Iu. — Prov.: curare cutem, i. e. to make much of oneself, H.

cyathus.definition: cyathus ī, m, ku/athos, a cup, drinking-cup, glass: cyathos sorbillans, T., H., Iu.—A measure, the 12th part of a sextarius, H.

cyclas.definition: cȳclas adis, f, kukla/s, a circular, white or purple state-robe, with a border, Pr., Iu.

cyclicus.definition: cȳclicus adj. kukliko/s, of a cycle: scriptor, a cyclic poet, one of the authors of the cycle of myths, H.

cycneus.definition: cycnēus (cȳgn-) adj., ku/kneios, of a swan: vox et oratio, i. e. the last speech.

cycnus.definition: cycnus or cȳgnus ī, m, ku/knos, the swan; celebrated for its singing, esp. when dying; consecrated to Apollo; a bird of good omen, V.; attached to the chariot of Venus, O.—Prov.: certent cycnis ululae, V.—A singer: Di…

cymbalum.definition: cymbalum ī, n (gen. plur. Cymbalūm, Ct.), ku/mbalon, a cymbal; two hollow plates of brass, which ring when struck together (used in festivals): cum domus cymbalis personaret, V., O., Ct., Iu.

cymbium.definition: cymbium ī, n, kumbi/on, a small drinking vessel, cup, bowl, V.

cynocephalus.definition: cynocephalus ī, m, kunoke/falos, an ape with a dog's head.

cyparissus.definition: cyparissus ī, f, kupa/rissos, a cypress-tree. —Plur.: coniferae, V.

cytisus.definition: cytisus ī, m, ku/tisos, a kind of clover, shrubby clover, V.

corium.definition: corium ī, n SCAL-, skin, hide, leather: bovis, Ta.: (animantes) coriis tectae: (turrīs) coriis intexerant, Cs.: scuta ex coriis, S.—Prov.: canis a corio numquam absterrebitur uncto, i. e. habits stick closely, H.

circumscripte.definition: circumscrīptē adv. circumscriptus, in periods: dicere: complecti singulas res.

carbaseus.definition: 'carbaseus adj. carbasus, of carbasus, of fine linen: vela: sinus, V.'

coacesco.definition: coacēscō acuī, —, ere, inch. com- + acesco, to become acid, sour: ut vinum, sic aetas vetustate coacescit.—Fig., to deteriorate, become corrupt.

catenatus.definition: catēnātus adj. catena, chained, fettered: Britannus, H.: ianitor, O.: taberna, fastened with a chain, Iu.

citra.definition: citrā adv. and praep. citer. I. Adv, on this side, on the hither side: (dextera) nec citra mota nec ultra, neither this way nor that, O.—On this side, nearer: id a capite arcessere: saepe etiam citra licet, not so far…

conlabefio.definition: con-labefīō (coll-) factus, fierī, pass, to fall to pieces, collapse, be ruined: ut (navis) conlabefieret, Cs.—Fig.: a Themistocle conlabefactus, overthrown, N.

clare.definition: clārē adv. with comp. clarus, brightly: fulgens, Ct. — Clearly, distinctly, plainly: gemere: dicere, H.: clare, ‘tuemini,’ inquit, Cs. — Fig., illustriously, honorably, splendidly: clarius exsplendescebat, N.: clarius…

compendiarius.definition: compendiārius (conp-) adj. compendium, short, easy: via ad gloriam.

conventum.definition: conventum ī, n 1 conventus, an agreement, compact, contract, convention: stare conventis: testes-conventorum, L.: pacti et conventi formula: Conventum et pactum, a marriage contract and settlement, Iu.

certe.definition: certē adv. with comp. certus, really, surely, assuredly, actually, certainly, as a fact: fuit certe id aequum: ea certe vera sunt, admitted facts: qui certius explorata referant, L.: Si reperire vocas amittere certius…

consitura.definition: cōnsitūra ae, f 1 consero, a sowing, planting: agri.

crebresco.definition: crēbrēscō bruī, —, ere creber, to become frequent, increase, spread abroad: crebrescunt optatae aurae, V.: horror, V.: sermo, V.: seditio, Ta.: crebrescit vivere Agrippam, it is generally reported, Ta.

coniunx.definition: coniūnx or coniux iugis, m and f com- + IV-, a married person, consort, spouse, husband, wife: coniuges et liberi: mulier cum suo coniuge: quo coniuge felix ferar, O.: mea: avara.—Of animals, the female, O.—A betrothe…

conloquium.definition: conloquium (coll-) ī, n conloquor, a conversation, conference, discourse: eo ad conloquium venerunt, Cs.: in Antoni conloquium venire: de pace in conloquium venire, S.: per conloquia de pace agere, Cs.: in conloquio e…

complusculi.definition: complūsculī (conp-) ae, a, adj. dim. complures, a good many, not a few: dies, T.

capillatus.definition: capillātus adj. with comp. capillus, having hair, hairy: bene, with a fine head of hair: capillatior quam ante: capillato consule, i. e. in the olden time, Iu.

colocasium.definition: colocāsium ī, n, koloka/sion, an Egyptian bean, marsh-lily, V.

centimanus.definition: 'centimanus adj. centum + manus, with a hundred hands (poet.): Gyas, H., O.'

circinus.definition: circinus ī, m, ki/rkinos, a pair of compasses: flumen Dubis, ut circino circumductum, Cs.

conclusum.definition: conclūsum ī, n P. n. of concludo, a conclusion (of a syllogism), inference.

corrupte.definition: corruptē adv. with comp. corruptus, perversely: iudicare: corruptius habiti, i. e. under less restraint, Ta.

coeptum.definition: coeptum ī, n coepio, a work begun, beginning, undertaking: nec taedia coepti Ulla mei capiam, O.: audax, L.: audacibus adnue coeptis, V.: temere coepta, L.: coeptis meis, O.: ne enuntiare coepta, L.

cylindrus.definition: cylindrus drī, m, ku/lindros, a cylinder,— A cylindrical stone for levelling, roller, V.—A precious stone in the form of a cylinder, Iu.

cingulus.definition: cingulus ī, m—Prop., a girdle, a zone (of the earth).

conloquens.definition: (conloquēns ntis), m P. of conloquor, one who converses; only plur: conloquentibus difficiles, i. e. avoiding interviews, L.

consolor.definition: cōn-sōlor ātus, ārī, dep., to encourage, animate, console, cheer, comfort: alqm, Cs.: alqm in miseriis: Piliam meis verbis, in my name: alqd consolandi tui gratiā dicere: me ipse illo solacio, quod, etc.: se per litte…

conlecticius.definition: conlēctīcius (coll-; not -titius) um, adj. conlectus, gathered in haste, huddled together: exercitus.

contumaciter.definition: contumāciter adv. with comp. contumax, obstinately, stubbornly: scribere: omnia agere, L.: contumacius se gerere, N.

ciris.definition: cīris is, f, kei=ris, a sea - bird, into which Scylla was changed, O.

creta.definition: crēta ae, f Creta, Cretan earth, pipe - clay, chalk, as a cosmetic, H.; for seals, C.; for cement, V.; eaten by serpents, V.: rapidus cretae Oaxes, turbulent, V.: cretā notati, i. e. with a mark of approval, H.

convenae.definition: convenae ārum, m and f com-+BA-, VEN-, assembled strangers, refugees, vagabonds: convenas congregasse: convenarum plebs, L.

confore.definition: cōnfore inf. com- + fore, inf fut. of sum, only impers, that it will be accomplished: et spero confore, i. e. to succeed, T.

compresse.definition: (compressē) adv. comprimo, briefly, succinctly; only comp. compressius loqui.

caeles.definition: (caeles) itis, adj. caelum, heavenly, celestial (not in nom sing.): agricolae, Tb.: regna, O.— Plur m. as subst, the gods, C., Ct.: rex caelitum, H.: cedere caelitibus, O.

Chimaerifera.definition: Chimaerifera adj. f Chimaera + 1 FER-, producing the Chimaera, O.

caris.definition: cāris idis, f, kari/s, a kind of sea-crab, O.

coliphia.definition: cōlīphia (coll-, cōlȳ-) ōrum, n, kwlu/fia, flesh-cakes (food for athletes), Iu.

creditum.definition: crēditum ī, n credo, a loan: solvere, L.: abiurare, S.

care.definition: cārē adv. with comp. carus, dearly, at a high price: emit carius, etc.: poema emere, H.

consors.definition: cōn-sors sortis, m and f I. Adj, having a common lot, of the same fortune: pectora (i. e. sorores), O.: sanguis, a brother's, O.: tecta, common, V.: casū s: fratres, partners: socius, H. — II. Subst, a sharer, co-heir…

colax.definition: 'colax acis, m a flatterer: parasitus colax, T.'

conductus.definition: (conductus ī),m P. of conduco. — Only plur, hirelings: operae conductorum: conducti plorant in funere, H. — Mercenary soldiers: conductorum III (milia), N.

canesco.definition: cānēscō —, —, ere, inch. caneo, to become hoary, grow gray, whiten: pabula canescunt (calore), O. — Fig., to grow old: (quercus) canescit saeclis. — Of style: cum oratio canesceret, was growing feeble.

conlaceratus.definition: 'con-laceratus (coll-) adj., torn to pieces: corpus, Ta.'

cogitatus.definition: cōgitātus adj. P. of cogito, deliberate: iniuria: verbum.

comice.definition: cōmicē adv. comicus, in the manner of comedy: res tragicas tractare.

compertus.definition: compertus adj. P. of comperio, ascertained, clearly known: quod de his duobus habuerint compertum: nobis ea res parum comperta est, S.— As subst n.: de his haud facile conpertum narraverim, exact information, S.

canephoros.definition: canēphoros f nom. plur. oe, acc. ōs, kanhfo/ros, a basket-carrier.— Plur., two statues, representing maidens carrying baskets on their heads, O.

Caeres.definition: Caeres itis or ētis, adj. Caere, of Caere: populus, L.: domus, V.— The people of Caere were Roman citizens, but without votes; hence, cera, the rolls of imperfect citizenship, to which Romans might be degraded by the …

circumlitus.definition: circum-litus P., spread over, smeared around, besmeared: taedis sulfura, O.: mortui cerā: saxa musco, covered, H.: (Midas) auro, bathed in gold, O.

culta.definition: 'culta orum, n 1 cultus, plantations, fields of grain: nitentia, V.: pinguia, V.'

coniuratio.definition: coniūrātiō ōnis, f coniuro, a uniting in an oath, sworn union, alliance: nobilitatis, Cs.: de bello, L.: (mulierum), common understanding, T. —A conspiracy, plot, secret combination: Catilinae, S.: impia, L.: coniurat…

consessus.definition: cōnsessus ūs, m consido, a collection (of persons), assembly: meorum iudicum: consessu maximo agere causam: consessum clamoribus implere, V.: a consessu plausus datus: se heros Consessu medium tulit (dat. for in conse…

cynicus.definition: cynicus adj., kuniko/s, Cynic: institutio, the Cynic philosophy, Ta.— As subst m., a Cynic philosopher, Cynic, C., H., Iu.: nudus, i. e. Diogenes, Iu.

conservans.definition: cōnservāns antis, adj. P. of conservo, preservative: eius statū s.

conveniens.definition: conveniēns entis, adj. P. of convenio, agreeing, consistent, corresponding: hunc superbum habitum convenientes sequebantur contemptūs aures, etc., L.: recta et convenientia natura desiderat: sibi convenientia finge, H…

culte.definition: cultē adv. with comp. cultus, elegantly: loqui, O.: cultius dicere, Ta.

culullus.definition: culullus ī, m a large drinking-vessel, beaker, bowl: aurei, H.: alqm multis urgere culullis, H.

capripes.definition: capripēs pedis, adj. caper + pes, goat-footed (poet.): Satyri, H.: Panes, Pr.

celebratus.definition: celebrātus adj. with comp. and sup. P. of celebro, frequented, thronged, much visited: forum, S. — Customary, usual, frequent: alqd in Graeco sermone.— Trite, familiar, notorious: res celebratissimae omnium sermone: c…

conserte.definition: cōnsertē adv. consertus, in close connection: omnia fieri.

Cilix.definition: Cilix icis, adj., *ki/lic, Cilician: Taurus, O. —Plur m., the Cilicians.

conficiens.definition: cōnficiēns ntis, adj. with sup. P. of conficio, efficient, producing: causae: civitas conficientissima litterarum. — Plur n. as subst: (bonorum) conficientia, the sources.

castigatus.definition: 'castigatus adj. P. of castigo, small, contracted: pectus, O.'

consentiens.definition: cōnsentiēns entis, abl. tī or te, adj. P. of consentio, agreeing, accordant, unanimous: senatus: rerum cognatio: hominum consentiente auctoritate contenti: clamore consentienti pugnam poscunt, L.

commemorandus.definition: 'commemorandus adj. P. of commemoro, memorable: iudicia.'

Cloacina.definition: Cloācīna or Cluācīna ae, f 2 CLV-, the purifier, a surname of Venus, L.

concluse.definition: conclūsē adv. concludo, with rhetorical finish: dicere.

conventicius.definition: conventīcius adj. 1 conventus, of assembling, for attendance; hence, as subst n. (sc. aes), money paid for attending an assembly.

citus.definition: 'citus adj. P. of cieo, quick, swift, rapid: classis, H.: navis, O.: mors, H.: incessus, S.: via, L.: quadrigae, V.: solvite vela citi (i. e. cito), V.: citus denatat, H.: ite citi, O.: equo, Ta.: remis, Ta.'

cupide.definition: cupidē adv. with comp. and sup. cupidus, eagerly, zealously, passionately, vehemently, ardently, gladly: alienos (agros) appetere: cupidius agmen insequi, Cs.: cupidissime populi amicitiam adpetere, Cs.—Ambitiously, i…

comitia.definition: comitia ōrum, n plur. of comitium, the Roman people in assembly, comitia curiata, of the patricians, held in the comitium, mainly to ratify or veto decrees of the senate: comitia fierent regi creando, L.; later only f…

conludo.definition: con-lūdō (coll-) sī, —, ere, to play together, sport with: paribus, H.—Poet.: videbis in aquā conludere plumas, move sportively, V. — Fig., to have a secret understanding: tecum.

coniugatio.definition: coniugātiō ōnis, f coniugo.—Prop., a connection; hence, the etymological connection of words.

constans.definition: cōnstāns antis, adj. with comp. and sup. P. of consto, firm, unchangeable, constant, immovable, uniform, steady, fixed, stable, invariable, regular, persistent: cursūs: constanti voltu, L.: aetas, mature: pax, uninter…

crater.definition: crātēr ēris (acc. -ēra), m, krath/r, a mixingvessel, wine-bowl, punch-bowl (poet.): Sistitur argento crater, O.: vertunt crateras aë nos, V.: urnae capax, holding three gallons, Iu. — A bowl: fuso crateres olivo, V.—T…

coetus.definition: coetus ūs, m for coitus, a coming together: amnium, Cu.—An assemblage, crowd, company: in omni coetu concilioque: sollemnes ludorum: nocturni, L.: socios in coetum Advocat, V.: coetu soluto, O.: coetibus alqd sancire,…

celox.definition: celōx ōcis, f 1 CEL-, a swift-sailing ship, cutter, yacht, L.

ciborium.definition: cibōrium ī, n, kibw/rion, a drinking-cup, H.

circumsonus.definition: 'circum-sonus adj., sounding around, filling with sound: turba canum, barking around, O.'

conlino.definition: con-linō (coll-) —, —, ere, to besmear, defile, pollute: crines pulvere, H.

crudeliter.definition: crūdēliter adv. with comp. and sup. crudelis, cruelly, fiercely, in a cruel manner, C.: excruciatus, Cs.: victoriam exercebant, S.: crudelius factum: amare, O.: supplicium crudelissime sumere.

congiarium.definition: congiārium ī, n congius, a largess to the poor of a congius to each man (of oil, etc.): congiariis multitudinem delenire.—A largess in money, gift, distribution: ab Antonio: plebi, Ta.: molitum, Cu.: multa, L.

clareo.definition: clāreō —, —, ēre clarus, to be bright, shine (of the stars), C. poet. — Fig., to be renowned, be illustrious: viri gloria claret, Enn. ap. C.

cuius.definition: cūius (old quōius) adj. 2 CA- —Interrog., of whom? whose? virgo quoiast? T.: cuium pecus? an Meliboei? V.—Relat., of whom, whose: is, cuia res sit.

conductum.definition: conductum ī, n conduco, something hired, the subject of a lease: alqd habere conducti, a hired apartment.

castoreum.definition: castoreum eī, n 1 castor, castoreum, a strong-smelling secretion of the beaver: virosa, V.

centumgeminus.definition: 'centumgeminus adj. centum + geminus, of multiple form: Briareus, i. e. with a hundred arms, V.'

concustoditus.definition: con-custōdītus P., closely watched, carefully guarded: a dracone, O.

citerior.definition: citerior ōris, and citimus, adj. comp. and sup. citer from cis, on this side: citerior provincia, Cs.: Hispania, C., N.—Nearer, next: (stella) ultima a caelo, citima terris.—Fig.: humana et citeriora considerat: ut ad…

coniungo.definition: con-iungō iūnxī, iūnctus, ere, to fasten together, connect, join, unite, gather: calamos cerā, V.: eam epistulam cum hac: huic (navi) alteram, Cs.: dextrae dextram, O.—Fig., to join, unite, associate: cohortes cum exe…

conlicio.definition: conliciō (coll-) —, —, ere com- + lacio, to mislead, beguile: me in breve tempus, T.

curate.definition: (cūrātē adj.), only comp, carefully, diligently: curatius disserere, Ta.: legi, between the lines, Ta.

Cyclops.definition: Cyclōps ōpis (acc. -ōpem or -ōpa), m, *ku/klwy (round-eye), a Cyclops, one of the fabulous giants on the coast of Sicily, C., V., H., O., Iu.: Cyclopa saltare, to imitate by pantomime, H.: moveri, H.—Plur., in later f…

compitalia.definition: compitālia iōrum compitum, n a festival in honor of the Lares.

Corus.definition: Cōrus ī, m the northwest wind; see Caurus.

censura.definition: cēnsura ae, f censor, the office of censor, censorship: tristis, L.: ad censuram petendam: magistra pudoris. — Prov.: Dat veniam corvis, vexat censura columbas, Iu. — Fig., a judgment, opinion: facilis censura cachinn…

comperendinatus.definition: comperendinātus ūs, m (C.), and comperendinātiō , ōnis, f (Ta.) comperendino, in law, an adjournment over one entire judicial day (required by law after pleading and before judgment).

comata.definition: comāta ae, adj. f coma, long-haired: Gallia, Transalpine Gaul: silva, in leaf, Ct.

curis.definition: curīs (quirīs) ītis Sabine, a spear, O.

commereor.definition: com-mereor (conm-) itus sum, ērī, dep., to commit, be guilty of: numquam quicquam erga me, T.

conversor.definition: con - versor ātus, ārī, to abide, frequent: in regiā , Cu.

cardaces.definition: cardaces um, m carda (Persian), warlike, a class of Persian soldiers; acc. Cardacas, N.

conlacrimatio.definition: conlacrimātiō (coll-) ōnis, f conlacrimo, a sympathetic weeping.

callum.definition: callum ī, n 2 CEL-, CER-, a hard skin, thick skin: mihi est calciamentum solorum callum: dissiluit percusso lammina callo, O.—Fig., insensibility, callousness: quasi callum obducere dolori, vetustatis.

cetera.definition: cētera adv. acc plur. of ceterus, for the rest, otherwise, in all else: praeter nomen cetera ignarus populi R., S.: hastile cetera teres praeterquam ad extremum, L.: hac in re unā dissimiles, at cetera paene gemelli, …

contemplor.definition: contemplor ātus, ārī, dep., to gaze at, view attentively, survey, behold, observe, contemplate: satis ut contemplata modo sis, T.: Contemplator item, cum, etc., V.: unumquemque vestrum: oculis pulchritudinem rerum: vo…

consilio.definition: cōnsiliō adv. abl. of consilium, intentionally, designedly, purposely: seu forte, seu consilio, L.: urbem Adferimur, V.

confidens.definition: cōnfīdēns entis, adj. with sup. P. of confido, bold, daring, confident: senex, T.—Shameless, audacious, impudent: Homo, T.: tumidusque, H.: astutia: iuvenum confidentissime, V.

cohaerens.definition: cohaerēns ntis, adj. P. of cohaereo, adjoining, continuous: aedificia, Ta. — Fig., consistent: apta inter se et cohaerentia: non cohaerentia inter se dicere, inconsistent assertions. — Harmonious: oratio.

candesco.definition: candēscō —, —, inch. candeo, to become bright, grow white, begin to glisten: aer solis ab ortu, O.: caput canis, Tb.—To begin to glow, grow red hot: currūs candescere sentit, O.

constiti.definition: cōnstitī perf. of consisto and of consto.

campester.definition: campester tris, tre, adj. campus, of a level field, even, flat, level: loci, Cs.: iter, L.: munitiones, field-works, Cs.: Scythae, dwelling on plains, H.: hostis, fighting on the open plain, L.—Plur n. as subst: pauca…

commoror.definition: com-moror (conm-) ātus, ārī, dep., to tarry, linger, abide, sojourn, remain, stay: illic tam diu, T.: dies XXV in eo loco, Cs.: Romae: apud alqm: commorandi natura devorsorium nobis dedit: paululum, S.—Of discourse, t…

conlibet.definition: (con-libet, conlubet, or collibet) buit or bitum est, ēre, impers, it pleases, is agreeable (only perf. system): si conlibuisset, H.: quae victoribus conlubuissent, S.: si quid conlubitumst, T.: simul ac mihi conlibit…

cornicen.definition: cornicen cinis, m cornu + 1 CAN-, a hornblower, trumpeter, cornet-player, C., S., L., Iu.

conlecta.definition: conlēcta (coll-) ae, f conlectus, a contribution, collection: a convivā exigere.

confutuo.definition: cōn-futuō —, —, ere, to cohabit with, Ct.

coniugo.definition: con-iugō āvī, ātus, āre, to join, unite: amicitiam, to form: coniugata verba, etymologically related.

criminor.definition: crīminor ātus, ārī, dep. crimen, to accuse of crime, complain of, impeach, calumniate: me tibi, T.: apud alqm nos: alios apud populum, L.—To complain of, charge, denounce: potentiam meam invidiose: nescio quid de illā…

consecratus.definition: cōnsecrātus adj. P. of consecro, hallowed, holy, sacred: locus, Cs.

collegium.definition: conlēgium or collēgium ī, n conlega, association in office, colleagueship: expertus mihi concordi collegio vir, L.: consul per tot collegia expertus, L.—An official body, association, board, bench, college, guild, cor…

conrumpo.definition: corrumpō (con-r-) rūpī, ruptus, ere, to destroy, ruin, waste: frumentum in areā: (frumentum) incendio, Cs.: coria igni, Cs.: ungues dentibus, to bite, Pr.: se suasque spes, S.: opportunitates, to lose, S.—To adulterat…

conmeo.definition: com-meō (conm-) āvī, ātus, āre, to go and come, pass to and fro, move back and forth, go about: ultro citro: tuto ab hostium incursu, Cs.: quā viā omnes commeabant, N.: illo mari, Ta.: ad ea furta quae reliquisses.—To…

cuncto.definition: cunctor (cont-) ātus, ārī, dep., to delay, linger, loiter, hesitate, doubt: cunctando restituit rem, Enn. ap. C.: cunctando bellum gerebat, L.: omnia si cunctor amitto: qui cunctatus fuerit, L.: dolo an vere, S.: mili…

conpono.definition: com-pōnō (conp-) posuī (-posīvī, Ta.), positus (-postus, V.), ere, to bring together, place together, collect, unite, join, connect, aggregate: in quo loco erant ea composita, quibus, etc.: aridum lignum, H.: duos ama…

conmuto.definition: com-mūtō (conm-) āvī, ātus, āre, to alter wholly, change entirely: signa rerum: quae commutantur fiuntque contraria: leges. — Fig.: ad commutandos animos.—To change, exchange, interchange, replace, substitute, barter,…

conmitto.definition: com - mittō (conm-) mīsī, missus, ere. I. To bring together, join, combine, put together, connect, unite: commissis operibus, L.: fidibusque commissa Moenia, O.: domus plumbo commissa, patched, In.: commissa inter se …

conminuo.definition: com-minuō (conm-) uī, ūtus, ere, to divide into small parts, break, crumble, crush, split: scalas, S.: anulum. — To lessen, diminish: argenti pondus, H.: opes civitatis. — Fig., to weaken, impair, violate: officium.— …

colloquium.definition: conloquium (coll-) ī, n conloquor, a conversation, conference, discourse: eo ad conloquium venerunt, Cs.: in Antoni conloquium venire: de pace in conloquium venire, S.: per conloquia de pace agere, Cs.: in conloquio e…

conpeto.definition: com - petō (conp-) —, —, ere, to coincide with, happen at the same time: tempora cum exitu Othonis, Ta.—To be adequate, be suitable, be fit: ad arma capienda, L.: neque oculis neque auribus, Ta.

crimino.definition: crīminor ātus, ārī, dep. crimen, to accuse of crime, complain of, impeach, calumniate: me tibi, T.: apud alqm nos: alios apud populum, L.—To complain of, charge, denounce: potentiam meam invidiose: nescio quid de illā…

conmoror.definition: com-moror (conm-) ātus, ārī, dep., to tarry, linger, abide, sojourn, remain, stay: illic tam diu, T.: dies XXV in eo loco, Cs.: Romae: apud alqm: commorandi natura devorsorium nobis dedit: paululum, S.—Of discourse, t…

circumvecto.definition: circumvector —, ārī, dep. circumveho, to ride about, sail around: oram, L.—Poet., to go through, describe: Singula, V.

commoro.definition: com-moror (conm-) ātus, ārī, dep., to tarry, linger, abide, sojourn, remain, stay: illic tam diu, T.: dies XXV in eo loco, Cs.: Romae: apud alqm: commorandi natura devorsorium nobis dedit: paululum, S.—Of discourse, t…

conpello.definition: 1) com - pellō (conp-) pulī, pulsus, ere, to drive together, drive in a body, collect, assemble: armentum in speluncam, L.: greges in unum, V.: pecus totius provinciae: (navīs) in portum, Cs.: adversarios intra moenia, N… | 2) compellō (conp-) āvī, ātus, āre 1 compello, to accost, address: alqm voce, V.: Hersiliam iussis vocibus: Tauream nomine, L.: Danaum verbis amicis, V. — To address reproachfully, reproach, chide, rebuke, upbraid, abuse…

collega.definition: conlēga or collēga ae, m com- + 3 LEG-, a partner in office, colleague, associate, assessor: in censurā: imperii, Ta.: conlegam habere: post me sedet, H.: dux delectus est, duo collegae dati, N. —An associate, compani…

collusor.definition: conlūsor (coll-) ōris, m conludo, a fellow gambler: suus.— A playmate: infans cum conlusore catello, Iu.

carnificor.definition: carnificō —, —, āre carnifex, to cut to pieces, mangle: carnificari (hostes) iacentes, L.

conmisceo.definition: com-misceō (conm-) miscuī, mīxtus (mīstus), ē re, to mix, mingle together, intermingle: ignem cum urbis incendio: frusta commixta mero, V.: Chio nota si commixta Falerni est, H.: fumus in auras Commixtus, V.— Fig., to…

commino.definition: com-minor (conm-) ātus, ārī, dep., to threaten, menace: pugnam, L.: inter se, L.

colloquor.definition: con-loquor (coll-) cūtus, ī, to talk, converse, confer, parley, hold a conversation: mecum, T.: cum homine: per Procillam (interpretam) cum eo, Cs.: cum eo de partiendo regno, N.: inter nos: de re p. multum inter se: …

conpremo.definition: com-primō (conp-) pressī, pressus, ere, to press together, bring together, compress, close: (digitos) compresserat pugnumque fecerat: labra, H.: oculos (of the dead), O.: murem, Ph.: ordines (of the army), to close, L…

convivo.definition: convīvor ātus, ārī, dep. conviva, to banquet, revel, carouse together: crebro, T.: in publico, de publico.

colluo.definition: con-luō luī, —, ere, to moisten, wet: ora, O.

conroboro.definition: corrōborō (con-r-) āvī, ātus, āre, to strengthen, invigorate, make strong, corroborate: vox cum se corroborarit: cum is iam se corroboravisset, i. e. was grown up.—Fig., to encourage, fortify, strengthen: virtutem: au…

conruo.definition: corruō (conr-) uī, —, ere com- + ruo, to fall together, fall down, fall, tumble, sink: aedes corruerunt: adducta funibus arbor, O.: igne rogus, O.: paene risu: exspirantes corruerunt, L.: quo loco corruerat icta (Hora…

conmoveo.definition: com-moveō (conm-) mōvī (commōrat, T.; commōrit, H.; commōssem, commōsset, commōsse, C.), mōtus, ēre. I. To put in violent motion, move, shake, stir: alas, V.: quis sese commovere potest? can stir: commovere se non sun…

commento.definition: 1) commentor ātus, ārī, intens. comminiscor, to meditate, think over, study, deliberate, weigh, prepare (mentally): commentandi causā convenire, deliberation: aliquid: causam: futuras mecum miserias: de populi R. liberta… | 2) commentor ōris, m com- + 1 MAN-, a deviser, discoverer: uvae, i. e. Bacchus, O.

conparo.definition: 1) com-parō (conp-) āvī, ātus, āre, to prepare, make ready, set in order, furnish, provide: ad magnitudinem frigorum sibi remedium: se, to get ready: se ad iter, L.: se ad omnīs casūs, Cs.: insidias Habito: dolum ad capi… | 2) comparō (conp-) āvī, ātum, āre compar, to bring together as equals, connect, pair, match, unite, join: donum dono contra, to set in opposition, T.: ea inter se: priore consulatu inter se conparati, L. — To bring toget…

conpingo.definition: compingō (conp-) pēgī, pāctus, ere com- + pango, to join together, frame, make by joining; only P. perf.: septem compacta cicutis Fistula, V.: harundinibus compacta fistula, O.—Fig., of the Stoic philos.: tam composit…

colligatio.definition: conligātiō (coll-) ōnis, f 2 conligo, a connection.— Plur., C.—Fig., a bond, union: causarum omnium: artior societatis.

collusio.definition: conlūsiō (coll-) ōnis, f conludo, a secret understanding, collusion: cum decumanis.

conporto.definition: com-portō (conp-) āvī, ātus, āre, to bring in, carry together, collect, accumulate, gather: argentum ad se: eo frumentum ex Asiā , Cs.: arma in templum: ad aggerem caespitibus conportandis, Cs.: aurum domum regiam, S.…

conplecto.definition: complector or conplector plexus, ī, dep. PARC-, PLEC-, to clasp, embrace, grasp: mulierem, T.: patrem: nepotes, V.: dextram euntis, V.: pedes, V.: membra lacertis, O.: inter nos: inter se, L.: Te comitem, V. — To gras…

collino.definition: con-linō (coll-) —, —, ere, to besmear, defile, pollute: crines pulvere, H.

collectio.definition: conlēctiō (coll-) ōnis, f conlectus, a collecting, gathering: (membrorum).—Fig., in rhet., a summing up, recapitulation.

curvor.definition: curvō āvī, ātus, āre curvus, to crook, bend, bow, curve, round: Curvari manūs et crescere in unguīs, O.: flexile cornu, O.: lances, i. e. by its weight, H.: Fronte curvatos imitatus ignīs lunae, the flaming sickle, H.…

conmisero.definition: com-miseror (conm-) ātus, ārī, dep., to commiserate, pity, bewail: fortunam Graeciae, N.: cum commiserari coeperit, to appeal for pity.

conpenso.definition: com-pēnsō (conp-) āvī, ātus, āre, to balance, make good, compensate, counterbalance: cum uno versiculo tot volumina laudum: laetitiam cum doloribus: bona cum vitiis, H.: damna ab isto aetatis fructu compensata, made u…

collatio.definition: conlātiō (coll-) ōnis, f conlatus, a bringing together, hostile meeting, collision: signorum.— A contribution, collection: decimae, L.: exempti conlationibus, Ta.—Fig., a comparison, similitude. —In philos.: rationis,…

collibet.definition: (con-libet, conlubet, or collibet) buit or bitum est, ēre, impers, it pleases, is agreeable (only perf. system): si conlibuisset, H.: quae victoribus conlubuissent, S.: si quid conlubitumst, T.: simul ac mihi conlibit…

colludo.definition: con-lūdō (coll-) sī, —, ere, to play together, sport with: paribus, H.—Poet.: videbis in aquā conludere plumas, move sportively, V. — Fig., to have a secret understanding: tecum.

conpareo.definition: com-pāreō (conp-) uī, —, ēre, to be evident, appear, be plain, be visible: vestigia, quibus exitūs eorum compareant: ut a naturā incohata compareant, may be seen.—To be present, be at hand, exist: signa et dona omnia:…

colluceo.definition: con-lūceō (coll-) —, —, ēre, to shine brightly, be brilliant, gleam, glow: sol, qui conluceat: conlucent ignes, V.: lampades undique, O.: (candelabri) fulgore conlucere templum: moenia flammis, V.: omnia luminibus, L.…

conplico.definition: com-plicō (conp-) āvī, ātus, āre, to fold together, fold up: epistulam.—Fig., to fold, roll up: animi complicata notio, involved.

cohorto.definition: co-hortor ātus, ārī, dep. com- + hortor, to animate, encourage, advise, incite, exhort, admonish: hac (eloquentiā) cohortamur: vim habere ad cohortandum: vos ad libertatem recuperandam: nostri cohortati inter se, Cs.:…

conplano.definition: com-plānō —, ātus, āre, to level, make even, raze: domum.

coacto.definition: coāctor ōris, m cogo, a collector (of money): perquiritur a coactoribus.— In an army, the rearguard: coactores agminis, Ta.

conrogo.definition: corrogō (conr-) āvī, ātus, āre com- + rogo, to bring together by entreaty, collect, drum up, obtain by soliciting: suos necessarios ab atriis: convenerunt conrogati: auxilia ab sociis, L.: vela cum antemnis ex navibus…

collecta.definition: conlēcta (coll-) ae, f conlectus, a contribution, collection: a convivā exigere.

conploro.definition: com-plōrō (conp-) āvī, ātus, āre, to bewail, lament loudly: penates, O.: mortui complorarentur, L.: morte comploratā: complorata res est p., despaired of, L.

collocutio.definition: conlocūtiō (coll-) ōnis, f conloquor, a conversation, conference, talk: hominum: familiarissimae cum alquo.

clango.definition: clangor ōris, m 1 CAL-, a sound, clang, noise: tubarum, V.: clangorem fundere (of birds), C. poët.: consonus (pennarum), O.: cum magno clangore volitare, L.

conrepo.definition: corrēpō (con-r-) psī, —, ere, to creep, slink: in aliquam onerariam.—Fig.: in dumeta, to take to the bush (i. e. unintelligible arguments).

conmemoro.definition: com-memorō (conm-) āvī, ātus, āre, to recall to memory, call to mind, be mindful of, keep in mind, remember: quid dixerim. — To bring to mind, remind of, recall: quid commemorem primum? T.: ea (facta), S.: ad commemor…

collaudo.definition: con - laudō (coll-) āvī, ātus, āre, to prize highly, extol: filium, T.: factum suis: militum virtutem, L.: alqm magnifice, L.: me, H.: conlaudatis militibus, Cs.: conlaudandus, quod, etc.

collecticius.definition: conlēctīcius (coll-; not -titius) um, adj. conlectus, gathered in haste, huddled together: exercitus.

collacrimatio.definition: conlacrimātiō (coll-) ōnis, f conlacrimo, a sympathetic weeping.

conmonstro.definition: com - mōnstrō (conm-) āvī, ātus, āre, to show, point out distinctly: parentīs mihi, T.: commonstrarier Mi istum volo, T.: aurum alicui: viam.

conmetior.definition: com-mētior (conm-) mēnsus, īrī, dep., to measure: siderum ambitūs inter se numero. — Fig., to measure, proportion: negotium cum tempore.

conpasco.definition: com-pāscō (con-) —, ere, to feed together, feed in common: ius est compascere.

circumcaedo.definition: circumcīdō cīdī, cīsus, ere circum + caedo, to cut around, cut, clip, trim: ars agricolarum, quae circumcidat: gladiis caespites, Cs.—Fig., to cut off, diminish, abridge, circumscribe, get rid of, abolish: multitudine…

conmemini.definition: com-meminī (conm-) isse, defect, to recollect clearly, remember well: hominem: sic, T.: me miserum (fuisse): Hac, si commemini, die, O.

conmiseresco.definition: com - miserēscō (conm-) —, —, ere, inch, to commiserate, have sympathy with. — Impers.: ipsam Bacchidem eius commiseresceret, even Bacchis would pity him, T.

conpungo.definition: com-pungō (conp-) nxī, nctus, ere, to prick severely, sting, prod, puncture: collum dolone, Ph.: compunctus notis Threïciis, tattooed. — Fig., to prick, goad: se suis acuminibus.

circumspector.definition: circumspectō āvī, ātus, āre, intens. circumspicio, to look about with attention, search around, look after: bestiae ut in pastu circumspectent: ora principum, L.: omnia: mare et silvas, Ta.: quānam ipse evaderet, L.: …

conteneo.definition: contineō tinuī, tentus, ēre com-+teneo, to hold together, bound, limit, comprise, enclose, surround, environ: ut trabes artē contineantur, Cs.: oppidum pons continebat, made a connection with, Cs.: hiberna milibus pas…

concado.definition: 1) concidō cidī, —, ere cado, to fall together, fall down, tumble, fall to earth: conclave illud concidit: urbs uno incendio: pinus bipenni, Ph.: ad terram, V.: sub onere, L.: concidere miratur arator tauros, O.—To fall … | 2) concīdō cīdī, cīsus, ere com- + caedo, to cut up, cut through, cut to pieces, ruin, destroy: nervos: navīs, L.: magnos scrobibus montīs, to break up mounds, V. — In battle, to cut to pieces, cut down, destroy, kill: m…

conmaculo.definition: com-maculō āvī, ātus, āre, to spot, stain, pollute, defile: sanguine manūs, V.—Fig., to disgrace, stain: se ambitu: se cum Iugurthā miscendo, S.

collaudatio.definition: conlaudātiō (coll-) ōnis, f conlaudo, warm praise, eulogy. hominis.

circumplecto.definition: circumplector —, ī, dep. circum + plecto, to clasp, embrace, surround, encompass: coniunctiones motu undique: domini patrimonium: pharetram auro, V.: (collem) opere, Cs.

commurmuro.definition: com-murmuror ātus, ārī, dep., to murmur in company: secum ipse.

conmingo.definition: com-mingō minxī, mictus (minctus), ere, to pollute, defile: lectum potus, H.: commicta lupa, Ct.: suavia salivā, Ct.

conmigro.definition: com-migrō (conm-) āvī, ātus, āre, to remove, migrate, enter: huc habitatum, T.: huc viciniae, T.: in tuam (domum): Romam, L.: e Germaniā in Gallias, Ta.

colliquefactus.definition: 'conliquefactus (coll-) P. com- + liquefio, dissolved, melted: (venenum) in potione.'

contesto.definition: con-testor ātus, ārī, dep., to call to witness, invoke, appeal to: deos, ut res feliciter eveniret, Cs.: caelum.—Of a suit at law, to introduce, set on foot, set at issue: litem.—Pass: lite contestatā .— Fig., to prov…

conmunio.definition: 1) com-mūniō (conm-) īvī (īvīsti or ī stī), ītus, īre, to fortify on all sides, secure, barricade, intrench: castella, Cs.: castra, L.: suos locos, S.: loca castellis idonea, N. — Fig., to make sure, strengthem: testimon… | 2) commūniō ōnis, f communis, a community, mutual participation, fellowship: inter alquos legis: sanguinis: litterarum: parietum, Ta.

conmercor.definition: com-mercor (conm-) ātus, ārī, dep., to buy up, purchase: arma, tela, S.

conmeto.definition: commētō (conm-) —, —, āre, freq. commeo, to visit habitually: ad mulierculam, T.

cubitor.definition: cubitō āvī, —, āre, freq. cubo, to lie down often, be accustomed to lie: tecum semper.

conmolio.definition: com-mōlior (conm-) ītus, īrī, dep., to set in motion, wield: dolum, Caecil. ap. C.

conpilo.definition: compīlō āvī, ātus, āre, to plunder, pillage, rifle, rob: fana: si malui compilari quam venire: hortos: te, H.: Crispini scrinia, H.: ipsum (Iovem), Ph.: ab iure consultis sapientiam, steal.

collustro.definition: con-lūstrō (coll-) āvī, ātus, āre, to illuminate, brighten, enlighten: sol omnia luce conlustrans: in picturis conlustrata, bright lights.—Fig., to survey, scrutinize, review: omnia oculis: cuncta equo, Ta.

conclaudo.definition: conclūdō sī, sus, ere com- + claudo, to shut up, close, imprison, enclose, confine: bestias: multitudinem: me in cellam cum illā , T.: illum aliquo, T.: locum sulco, V.: Suave locus voci resonat conclusus, H.: conclus…

conrodo.definition: corrōdō (conr-) sī, sus, ere com- + rodo, to gnaw, gnaw to pieces: scuta: ossa, Iu.—To wear away (of a file): ferrum, Ph.

conmereo.definition: com-mereō (conm-) uī, itus, ēre, to merit fully, deserve, incur, earn: aliquam aestimationem: ut caperet odium illam mei, T.: poenam, O.— To commit, be guilty of, perpetrate: culpam, T.: alqd, T., O.

conmitigo.definition: com-mītigō (conm-) —, —, āre, to make soft, mellow: tibi sandalio caput, T.

Centaurus.definition: 1) Centaurus ī, m a Centaur, a fabled monster, half man, half horse, V., H., O.—Esp., Chiron, H.—A ship's figure-head, V.—A southern constellation. | 2) Centaurus ī, f the ship Centaur, V.

cupido.definition: 1) Cupīdō inis, m the god of love, Cupid, son of Venus, C., V., O., H. — Plur: mater Cupidinum, H. | 2) cupīdō inis, f (poet. also m) CVP-, a desire, wish, longing, eagerness, passion: cepit me proloqui: urbis condendae, L.: somni, S.: gloriae, S.: cupidinibus statuere modum, H.: si vobis cupido Certa sequi, resolve, V.…

caligo.definition: 1) cālīgō inis, f 2 CAL-, a thick air, mist, vapor, fog: picea, V.: atra, V.: noctem eadem caligo obtinuit (i. e. nebula), L.: Boreas caligine tectus, i. e. dust and clouds, O.—Meton., darkness. obscurity, gloom: cum alt… | 2) cālīgō —, —, āre 1 caligo, to steam, reek, darken: caligans (Centaurus): (nubes) umida circum Caligat, V.—Meton., to be dark, gloomy: caligans nigrā formidine lucus, V.: altae caligantesque fenestrae, dizzy, Iu.

calo.definition: 1) cālō —, ātus, āre 1 CAL-, to call together, summon, convoke (only of religious assemblies); hence, a calatis Gaviis, by the assembled gens Gavia. | 2) cālō ōnis, m a servant in the army, soldier's servant, Cs.: turba calonum, L.—A low servant, drudge: plures calones Pascendi, H.

cassis.definition: 1) cassis idis, f SCAD-, a helmet of metal: muliones cum cassidibus, Cs.: equinis Fulva iubis, O.: caelata, Iu.—Poet.: aetas patiens cassidis, i. e. of war, Iu. | 2) cassis is, m SCAD-, a hunting-net, snare, toil: viso casse, O.—Usu. plur: (cervos) cassibus agitare, V.: ponere, O.—A spider's web: in foribus suspendit aranea casses, V.

castra.definition: 1) castra see castrum. | 2) castra ōrum, n a military camp, encampment (regularly a square surrounded by a trench, and a wall with four gates): stativa, permanent: hiberna, L.: navalia, an encampment to protect a landing, Cs.: nautica, N.: bina:…

catella.definition: 1) catella ae, f dim. catulus, a female puppy, young bitch, Iu. | 2) catēlla ae, f dim. catena, a little chain, H., L.

cedo.definition: 1) cēdō cessī, cessus, ere 1 CAD-, to go from, give place, remove, withdraw, go away, depart, retire: cedam atque abibo: ex ingratā civitate: patriā: carinā, Ct.: per ora (hominum), i. e. to be seen, H.: Siciliā sibi omn… | 2) cedo plur. cette, old imper, hither with it, give, bring here: Puerum, mihi cedo, T.: senem, bring hither, T.: cedo, quaeso, codicem: cedo tabulas.— Esp., let us hear, tell, say, speak, out with it: cedo istuc tuom co…

census.definition: 1) cēnsus P. of censeo. | 2) cēnsus ūs, m censeo, a registering of citizens and property by the censors, census, appraisement: censum habere: agere, L.: censu prohibere, to exclude from the list of citizens.—A counting, numbering: eorum, qui domu…

centurio.definition: 1) centuriō āvī, ātus, āre centuria, to divide into centuries, assign to companies, organize (of infantry): homines centuriari: iuventutem, L.: centuriati pedites, L. | 2) centuriō ōnis, m centuria, a commander of a century, captain, centurion (next in rank to the tribunes of the legion), C., S., L., H.: primi pili, of the first maniple (of the triarii), the first centurion of the legio…

cereus.definition: 1) cēreus adj. cera, waxen, of wax: nihil: effigies, H.: neque proponi cereus opto, offered for sale in (a statue of) wax, H.: castra, i. e. honeycomb, V.: regna, realms of bees, V.—Wax-colored: pruna, V.—Pliant, soft: b… | 2) cēreus ī, m 1 cereus, a wax-light, taper.

certo.definition: 1) certō adv. certus, with certainty, certainly, surely, of a truth, in fact, really: nihil ita exspectare quasi certo futurum: ego rus abituram me esse certo decrevi, T.—With scio, I know fully, it is beyond doubt: hoc … | 2) certō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. certus, to match, vie with, fight, contend, struggle, combat, do battle: armis cum hoste, an venenis?: pugnis, calcibus: proelio, S.: de salute, Ta.: de ambiguo agro bello, L.: acie, V.: an…

cinctus.definition: 1) cīnctus P. of cingo. | 2) cīnctus ūs, m cingo, a girding: Gabinus, a manner of girding the toga: incinctus cinctu Gabino, L.: cinctu Gabino Insignis, V.

circuitus.definition: 1) circuitus P. of circumeo. | 2) circuitus or circumitus ūs, m circumeo, a going round, circling, revolving, revolution. solis. — A circuit, compass, way around: quod interiore spatio minorem circuitum habebant, Cs.: parvo circuitu locum petere, L.: …

circumiectus.definition: 1) circumiectus adj.
